tagline: Up the McKenzie from the farm plains toward the firs.
intro: OR 126 leaves the farm country east of Eugene and follows the McKenzie upstream toward the fir forests of the Cascades, zigzagging along the bank of a river known for its fly-fishing. Past Leaburg the river slows behind a dam into Leaburg Lake, and past Vida it runs wilder again, through boulder fields and Class III rapids.
The McKenzie drift boat came from this river in the 1930s, a dory built to run the rocky water and give an angler a steady place to stand and cast.
season: Travel Oregon lists it as a year-round drive.

moments.title: Leaburg
moments.text: Upstream, Leaburg Dam diverts the river into a canal that runs about five miles above its natural level to spin the turbines of an Art Deco powerhouse.

moments.title: Goodpasture Bridge
moments.text: Built in 1938, the second longest covered bridge in Oregon still carries logging trucks, and the 2020 rumor that wildfire had destroyed it proved false.

moments.title: Finn Rock
moments.text: The rock looks like a shark's fin but is named for Ben Finn, known as the biggest liar on the McKenzie, who claimed he was the model for Huckleberry Finn.
